editorial:
Imagine working in a place where the adults are supposed to protect the kids, but some of those adults are the ones you should actually fear. You follow Eva, a kind teacher at a juvenile detention center who notices something is very wrong. After a scary incident happens between a guard and one of the boys, the official story just doesn't add up. You get to feel Eva's stress as she tries to uncover the truth while dealing with a system that wants to keep things quiet. It feels heavy and tense, making you wonder who you can actually trust in a building full of secrets.

The acting is top notch and makes the drama feel real rather than staged. While the pace starts a bit slow, the tension builds up until you are practically leaning forward in your seat. If you like stories about fighting for the underdog, you will love this.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Eva discovers that the guard was indeed abusive and that the system helped cover it up. The tension peaks when the truth finally comes out, leading to a confrontation that exposes the corruption within the center. It ends on a bittersweet note, showing that while some justice is served, the scars left on the young boys will take a long time to heal. You see a shift in power as the victims finally find their voice.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gripping dramas about justice and truth.
